page: Microsoft Azure L32as_v3 is a storage and memory-optimized server belonging to the LASv3 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The configuration features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Memory capacity stands at 256.0 GB, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of an 8008 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2847.38 and Geekbench image processing scoring 14374.0, both placing in the top 25%. Passmark memory performance is also strong at 2852.32. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, with uncached read bandwidth at 79.55 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 45.38 GB/sec. Large-scale workloads like LLM inference on a 70B model show weak performance at 6.58 tokens/sec, highlighting a tradeoff for massive AI model execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high local NVMe storage density and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio offer solid value for data-intensive workloads without the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware. The server is optimized for database hosting, large-scale file systems, data warehousing, and memory-intensive applications that benefit from high-capacity local NVMe storage and strong single-core execution.
